challenges.name: find-the-missing-800ms-evidence
challenges.title: Find the Missing 800 ms: read the evidence
challenges.description: POST /submissions takes 1,240 ms but its child spans cover only about 440 ms. Six statements on one evidence pack - the slow trace (A), a second trace found by submission id (B), the request's logs (C), the code (D) and the Collector's own metrics (E) - take you from reading the evidence to a hypothesis, past two wrong explanations, to the scope of the fix and its verification.

questions.question:
Evidence A - the slow trace (service submissions-api, host api-7f9c):
Trace 4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736
Span                          Start      End        Duration   Self time
POST /submissions             0 ms       1,240 ms   1,240 ms   802 ms
  auth.verify                 1 ms       35 ms      34 ms      34 ms
  submissions.validate        35 ms      57 ms      22 ms      22 ms
  cache.get problem:p_42      57 ms      66 ms      9 ms       9 ms
  INSERT submissions          866 ms     1,124 ms   258 ms     258 ms
  send grading                1,124 ms   1,239 ms   115 ms     115 ms

Statement: "The children of POST /submissions cover about 440 ms of its 1,240 ms, and almost all of the uncovered time is one stretch: the 800 ms between the end of cache.get and the start of INSERT submissions."
questions.explanation: True. The children do not overlap, so their covered time is the plain sum: 34 + 22 + 9 + 258 + 115 = 438 ms. The root's self time of 802 ms is 1,240 - 438, and 800 ms of it lies between 66 ms (cache.get ends) and 866 ms (INSERT starts); the remaining 2 ms are the first millisecond and the last one. Locating the hole precisely is the first step: it tells you which code to read. The common mistake is to read a large root self time as "the root's own code is slow" without checking where the uncovered time sits.

Evidence C - the request's logs (submission_id = sub_9f2):
14:03:12.000 info request started            trace_id=4bf92f35... route="POST /submissions"
14:03:12.066 info calling plagiarism service trace_id=4bf92f35... bytes=1840
14:03:12.866 info plagiarism verdict         verdict=clean took_ms=800
14:03:13.240 info request finished           trace_id=4bf92f35... status=202 duration_ms=1240

Statement: "The missing 800 ms were recorded: the plagiarism call has a span, but it was started where no context was active, so the SDK gave it a trace of its own instead of making it a child of POST /submissions."
questions.explanation: True. B's span starts at .066 and lasts 800 ms, exactly the hole in A (66 ms to 866 ms), with the same submission id from the same service and host, and it has no parent. C confirms the call at .066 and the verdict at .866, and the verdict line has no trace_id: when it was written, no span was active. The 18,412 orphan roots against 18,430 requests show it happens on practically every submission. The time is not missing; it is attached to the wrong trace. The misconception is that a hole in a trace means time nobody measured.

Evidence B - search submission.id = sub_9f2:
Trace 7d1c09e4b2a54f8e9c3b6a1d0f2e4c58 (service submissions-api, host api-7f9c)
plagiarism.check   start 14:03:12.066   duration 800 ms   parent: none (root span)
  attributes: submission.id=sub_9f2  plagiarism.verdict=clean
Root spans named plagiarism.check, last 24 h: 18,412
Root spans named POST /submissions, last 24 h: 18,430

Statement: "The Collector dropped the plagiarism span under load; increasing the exporter's queue size would put it back under POST /submissions."
questions.explanation: False. E shows nothing refused, nothing failed and a queue at 12 of 5,000. More decisively, B shows the span reached the backend: it was not dropped, it is a root span in another trace. The parent of a span is decided in the process, by the context active when the span starts; the Collector forwards spans and cannot re-parent them. A dropped span looks different: it is missing everywhere, and its own children (if any) show a parent id that no span in the trace has. The misconception is to blame the pipeline for every gap before searching for the missing operation.

Evidence C - the request's logs (submission_id = sub_9f2):

14:03:12.066 info calling plagiarism service trace_id=4bf92f35... bytes=1840
14:03:12.866 info plagiarism verdict         verdict=clean took_ms=800
14:03:13.240 info request finished           trace_id=4bf92f35... status=202 duration_ms=1240

Statement: "The gap is an artefact of clock skew: the API host's clock and the clock that timed the plagiarism call disagree by about 800 ms."
questions.explanation: False. Clock skew shifts spans recorded by different machines against each other. Every span in A and B is recorded by service submissions-api on host api-7f9c, and every line in C comes from the same process: one clock. The logs agree with the spans on their own terms (took_ms=800, duration_ms=1240), and the plagiarism service's own clock appears nowhere in this evidence. The misconception is to reach for skew whenever times do not add up, even when everything was measured by the same process.

False. A shows INSERT submissions and send grading as children of POST /submissions, in the right trace. They run after await this.checkPlagiarism(...), and an await continuation resumes in the context of the async function that awaited, whoever resolved the promise. Only the code inside the callback runs in the context of the client's connection, which was opened at startup with no span active. The fix belongs where the context is lost: bind the callback passed to check (or start the span before the call). The misconception is to spread context.bind over code that never lost its context, which hides where the real boundary is.

True. Each check matches one symptom in the evidence: the child closes the hole in A, the self time measures that nothing else is missing, the orphan count from B should drop to zero for requests served by the new version, and the log line from C proves the callback now runs in the request's context. Add a regression test with an in-memory exporter (two concurrent submissions, each check under its own request) so the next refactor of the client cannot bring the hole back. The misconception is to verify by eye on a single trace and stop there.

challenges.name: find-the-missing-800ms
challenges.title: Find the Missing 800 ms
challenges.description:
Since the plagiarism check was added, traces of POST /submissions on CodeDev have a hole: the root span is 1,240 ms long but its children cover about 440 ms, and every request also creates a separate trace whose root is "plagiarism.check", with the same submission id and the same timing. The trace report has a second problem: its self time column shows negative or too small values for spans whose children run in parallel or keep running after the span ends.

The file contains a context API on top of AsyncLocalStorage (context.active(), context.with(), context.bind(); await and promises carry the context by themselves), a tiny tracer, a fake clock and the plagiarism client, which keeps one connection and calls your callback from code that runs outside any request. Fix the app code so that:
- every plagiarism.check span is a child of the POST /submissions span of the request that made the call, also when several requests are in flight;
- selfTime returns the part of the span's own [start..end] that none of its children covers: overlapping children count once, and the part of a child outside its parent does not count.

Input (stdin): { "submissions": [{ "id", "startAt", "plagiarismMs", "steps" }] }. A step is "name:ms" (a span with ms of fake I/O), "plagiarism" (the plagiarism check, at most one per submission), "&<step>" (started but not awaited) or an array of steps run with Promise.all.
Output: every trace as a tree, one span per line: name, the submission id when the span has one, [start..end] in fake ms and self=<self time>; children sorted by start, then end, then name. Do not change the context, the tracer, the clock, the plagiarism client or the test runner.
hints: Where is plagiarism.check started, and which context is active at that exact moment? Who calls that code: the request, or the client's connection?

Two places: the callback passed to plagiarismClient.check (the context API in the file has a way to carry the caller's context into a function that someone else calls later), and the loop in selfTime that subtracts child durations. Draw two children [20..30] and [20..45] under a parent [0..60]: what should self time be?

A similar computation on other data: a room is booked [9..12], [10..11] and [11..14]; the time it is busy within a working day [8..13] is the length of the union of the bookings clipped to the day: [9..13] = 4 hours, not 3 + 1 + 3 = 7. Sort the intervals by start, clip each to the day and merge the ones that overlap before adding lengths.
